name: GitLab CI
description: Protects against destructive GitLab CI/CD operations like deleting variables, \ removing artifacts, and unregistering runners.

destructive_patterns.name: glab-variable-delete
destructive_patterns.description: glab variable delete removes CI variables and can break pipelines.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a GitLab CI/CD variable removes it from the project, group, or instance. \ Pipelines that depend on this variable will fail with undefined variable errors. \ Protected or masked variable values cannot be recovered after deletion.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - glab variable list: Review existing variables first \ - Update variable value instead of deleting \ - Check .gitlab-ci.yml for variable usage before removing

destructive_patterns.name: glab-ci-delete
destructive_patterns.description: glab ci delete removes pipeline artifacts or pipelines.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting pipelines or artifacts removes build history, job logs, and generated \ files. This affects debugging capabilities and audit trails. Artifacts needed \ for deployments or releases will no longer be available.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - glab ci list: Review pipelines before deletion \ - glab ci view: Inspect pipeline details \ - Download artifacts before deletion if needed

destructive_patterns.name: glab-api-delete-variables
destructive_patterns.description: glab api DELETE against variables endpoints removes CI variables.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Making DELETE requests to GitLab variables API removes CI/CD variables directly. \ This bypasses CLI confirmations and immediately affects all pipelines using these \ variables. Protected variable values cannot be recovered.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use glab variable delete for safer deletion \ - GET request first: Verify variable exists \ - Prefer CLI commands over direct API calls

destructive_patterns.name: gitlab-runner-unregister
destructive_patterns.description: gitlab-runner unregister removes runners and can halt CI.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Unregistering a GitLab runner removes it from the GitLab instance. Jobs assigned \ to this runner will be stuck pending or fail. With --all-runners, all runners \ on the machine are removed, potentially halting all CI/CD for multiple projects.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gitlab-runner list: Review registered runners first \ - Pause the runner in GitLab UI instead \ - Verify replacement runners are available before removing
